clue.text: Fresh air and Chianti drinking encountered in summer?

definitions.note: read as one who sums, a person doing sums

indicators.note: drinking means the rearranged letters take in another piece, which goes inside them
fresh signals the letters of the two words are made new, rearranged

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: A refreshing drink of Italian wine in the open air, enjoyed on a summer's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges AIR and CHIANTI into ARITHICIAN, which 'drinking' takes in. 'summer' is not the season but someone who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does sums is a person skilled with numbers, a mathematician of arithmetic.

clue.text: Fan of ceremonies last to leave hotel with posh celebs

indicators.note: the final letter of the hotel's name is dropped

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone who loves grand occasions sweeps out of a smart hotel with high-society stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to leave' drops Z from RITZ, leaving RIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to formal rites and observances is a lover of ceremonial practice.

clue.text: Handle drug put in acid the wrong way

indicators.note: the drug letter is put inside the reversed word
the word for acid is read backwards, the wrong way in a down clue

parts.note: acid as a taste means tart, sour
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Instructions for handling a drug that has been added to acid incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns TART into TRAT, and 'put in' places E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or a person is to deal with them, a synonym of handle as a verb.

clue.text: Native islander to wander around on island

indicators.note: around turns the word for wander back to front

parts.note: to wander is to roam

explanation.surface: An indigenous islander roams about on their island home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, an island nation.

clue.text: Special unit's request to mine ground etc

indicators.note: to mine is to dig into, so the request phrase goes inside the rearranged letters
ground, as in ground up, signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: to request is to ask for

explanation.surface: A special unit seeks permission to dig the ground and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges the abbreviation for et cetera into TCE, which the request phrase mines into.
explanation.definitionFit: A group formed for a particular operation or job is a special unit, often military or police.

clue.text: Corresponding with Italian chap covering rugby

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with

indicators.note: covering means the word for chap goes round the rugby letters

parts.note: a chap is a gent
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: An Italian man who writes about, or reports on, rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes or quantities that agree or match exactly are in correspondence, as in geometry.

clue.text: A foreign greeting when turning up?

definitions.text: A foreign greeting when turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the letters bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: hola is Spanish for hello

explanation.surface: A puzzle about saying hello abroad whenever you arrive somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses A plus HOLA. The whole clue is also the definition: a Hawaiian hello, said on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word is used as both hello and goodbye, so it is a non-English salutation.

clue.text: English author's cross — really cross — with university

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
really cross means angry, mad
Oxford is the famous English university

explanation.surface: A writer is crossed, then very crossed, about a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'cross' first means wading across, then means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist who wrote The Good Soldier and Parade's End was an English writer.

clue.text: Oddly ingenious PM's working to engage crime-fighting assistant

indicators.note: to engage means to take in, so the sidekick goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister; with the 's it gives a possessive form
Robin is Batman's sidekick
working means on, in operation

explanation.surface: A prime minister cleverly signs up a sidekick to help fight crime.
explanation.walkthrough: William Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist of absurd contraptions, so his name describes overcomplicated gadgetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a British byword for absurdly elaborate contraptions, so it describes eccentric cleverness.

clue.text: Not working hard? I will be active

indicators.note: working signals the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: An idle person promises to get busy soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not working' looks like idle, but 'working' rearranges NOT into ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly busy or moving about is an idiom for being active.

clue.text: Faint report of crime by policeman close to scene

definitions.note: a noun here: a faint, a swoon

indicators.note: report suggests the word is heard, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: a sin is a crime or wrongdoing
a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A policeman, arriving at a crime scene, collapses at the report.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term is a temporary loss of consciousness, a fainting fit.

clue.text: Leader of Republicans plugging inane plan

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, going inside the silly word

parts.note: inane means daft

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter

explanation.surface: The head of the Republicans is pushing a foolish scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a sketch of a proposal.

clue.text: Hip name in design for person shopping

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in

indicators.note: in means the name letter goes inside the word for design

parts.note: a format is a layout or design

explanation.surface: A trendy name on a design for a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping' is not buying goods but shopping someone, informing on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone in British slang is to betray them to the authorities, as a grass does.

clue.text: European comrade has another try

parts.note: another European comrade: ami is French for friend
a go is a try

explanation.surface: A friend from Europe has one more attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another European comrade, the French AMI, beside the Spanish answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for friend makes a pal from Spain a continental companion.

clue.text: Concerned with odour, emptied overfull workplace

indicators.note: emptied means removing the inside letters, leaving the outer pair

parts.note: a factory is a workplace

explanation.surface: A complaint about the smell of an overcrowded workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the sense of smell, which is concerned with scents.

clue.text: This guy's skill welcomed by drinking party

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken inside the word for a drinking session

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art means skill

explanation.surface: A man's talents are appreciated at a boozy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This guy' points at the person who would be serving at a drinking party.
explanation.definitionFit: The person behind the bar serving drinks is the guy the clue points to.

clue.text: Removal of Bush or Blair, unfortunately associated with Nazi

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A political smear: getting rid of Bush or Blair, sadly linked to a Nazi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president but is body hair; the answer is a kind of bikini wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A full bikini wax that strips away all pubic hair is named after a South American country.

clue.text: Right pig stocked by man who's bred bull here?

indicators.note: stocked by means held inside the word for father

parts.note: a man who has bred, a father, is a dad
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A farmer who breeds bulls also keeps a proper pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is not a farm animal but the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull, or bullseye, is the centre of the circular board aimed at in darts.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy not having a partner

definitions.meaning: literally without a date, someone to go out with

explanation.surface: An old fogey with no partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means old-fashioned, and read literally means lacking someone to go out with.

clue.text: Taoiseach's content to go and pinch pound

indicators.note: the contents of the word are removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, rob

explanation.surface: The Irish leader is happy to leave and steal a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the Irish prime minister. 'content' is not happy but the inside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to beat rhythmically, as a pulsing heart or headache does.

clue.text: Attentive to detail, if back committing crime

indicators.note: back means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: nicking is stealing, a crime

explanation.surface: A meticulous criminal, if only they went back to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overly fussy and particular means fussing over small details.

clue.text: Coward's boxing very unorthodox

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright

explanation.surface: A boxing style that is very unusual for a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is not a timid person but the playwright Noel Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new and original is not conventional, hence unorthodox.

clue.text: Fire fellow following foolishness

indicators.note: following means the fellow letter comes after

parts.note: a goof is a silly blunder

explanation.surface: A man is sacked after his blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like sack but means discharge, as a gun does.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun or alarm that discharges is said to explode or sound off, which is to fire.

clue.text: Part of boat or vessel keeps swinging both ways

indicators.note: a vessel that keeps something holds it within, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel
slang for bisexual, bi

explanation.surface: A boat part rocks from side to side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a room on a ship or boat, where passengers or crew sleep.

clue.text: Native American wraps papa eats in France

indicators.note: wraps means surrounds the other letter

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Native American wrapping food for their dad while in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin French pancake is a typical food served in France.

clue.text: Filled envelopes a fiddle to fill in US state

indicators.note: to fill means going inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island
a viol is an old stringed instrument, a fiddle

explanation.surface: Stuffed envelopes as part of a swindle in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pasta parcels with a stuffing are filled envelopes of dough.

clue.text: No-go area hasn't a twining aromatic plant

indicators.note: hasn't means the single letter is taken out of the pool of letters
twining, twisting together, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forbidden zone lacks a climbing scented plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A from NOGOAREA and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb used in Mediterranean cooking is a fragrant plant related to marjoram.

clue.text: Grassy areas acting as WC?

parts.note: acting means playing a role
W.C. Fields was an American comic actor

explanation.surface: Grassy spaces doing duty as a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'WC' is not a toilet but the comedian W.C. Fields: acting as him is playing Fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports grounds of grass where games are played are open grassed spaces.
